units.translation: [ἔσω [within] is more regular than εἴσω [within], as Apollonius on adverbs p. 577, 24, the scholia on Dionysius Thrax p. 942, 33, and Helladius in Photius' Bibliotheca p. 533, 27 have said, although there at line 10 he said ἐς [into] is more regular than εἰς [into], whose principle is almost the same. For the comic poets never said ἔσω [within], as is shown in the Thesaurus vol. 3 p. 343, but the tragedians not only said εἴσω [within], but also ἔσω [within], where the iambic meter required it. In Aeschylus, εἴσω [within] is read when the meter demands it in the iambic trimeter Sept. 560, in the anapests fr. 128, but ἔσω [within] in the iambic trimeters Ag. 1343, Ch. 553, 919, 921. Where the meter allows either spelling, in M sometimes εἴσω [within] sometimes ἔσω [within] is read, as the examples to be cited below show, in which I have preserved the manuscript reading, although in the text in such places I have consistently written εἴσω [within]. The other adverb of the same root, which is rarely read in the tragedians, is so consistently written ἔσωθεν [from within] that very few examples of the other spelling εἴσωθεν [from within] are found, on which see the Thesaurus vol. 3 p. 343] εἴσω [within] means 'inside', and differs from ἔνδον [within], which means 'within', although this distinction is sometimes neglected, on which Lobeck on Phrynichus p. 127 and, as far as the epic poets are concerned, Lehrs on the Studies of Aristarchus p. 134 second edition have spoken. In Aeschylus it means 'inside'
[But there at line 790 ἔσω [within] is corrupt for ἔσωθεν [from within].]
[Ch. 1059 in M εἰσω (εἰσσ᾽ ὁ [one and the] by a corrector) καθαρμός [purification], where Erfurdt rightly reads εἷς σοι καθαρμός [one purification for you].]
To nourish evils by letting the tongue flow inside the gates.
The image – the one from outside will blame the bearer inside.
I have been struck with a fatal blow within.
You have drunk beforehand – inside the tent.
Do not hold out profit to me and then deprive me of it.
where either another εἴτε [whether] or εἴτ᾽ οὐν [or else] has preceded or followed.
The first εἴτε [whether] is sometimes omitted.
if Hermann correctly corrected it thus for ὁ γοῦν [he at least], which is in Stobaeus 125, 7.
Whether having learned something good or not.
Whether he himself was present near the dying man, or speaks having learned from an obscure report.
Whether he sets his foot in the regions of the Libyan land, or surveys the Phlegraean plain.
Whether true or in the manner of dreams – the light has deceived the mind.
Whether I speak about one dead or alive.
Whether the opinion of friends will prevail to bring him back, or to bury him.
Or else a sophist greatly playing false on the lyre,
But whether you wish to praise or blame me, it is all the same.
Whether she was born a moray eel or a viper.
Whether with a band of soldiers or alone.
Whether justly or not, judge the case.
